title: Session Probe Playbook — runtime proxy for session annotation
content:
Purpose:
Lightweight, opt-in runtime 'probe' that sits next to client-facing session gateways and annotates or samples session traffic for debugging, telemetry, and privacy-safe inspection. Not a full recorder — focused on stamps, metadata enrichment, and short-lived snapshot payloads.

Goals (quick):
- Give engineers a low-friction way to inspect hard-to-repro LLM session failures without shipping full conversation logs to S3.
- Maintain privacy boundaries: redaction hooks, token-level hashing, configurable retention windows.
- Minimal latency impact (<= 4ms p50 added) and safe fail-open behavior.

Operational modes:
- off: no probe actions
- sample: probabilistic sampling (configurable rate per-route)
- on-demand: sample only when a trace flag is active (via header or control-plane switch)
- annotate-only: enrich request/response with stamps and feature vectors but do NOT persist full text

High-level flow (ascii):
Client -> Gateway -> Session Probe (inline) -> Runtime
                        |
                        +-> Control plane (probe policy, redaction rules, keys)

API shapes (sketch, json-as-text):
- POST /v1/probe/annotate  {
    "session_id": "string",
    "route": "string",
    "event": "request|response|error",
    "stamps": { "latency_ms": 12, "tokens": 56 },
    "features_base64": "..."  // optional compressed feature bag
  }

- POST /v1/probe/snapshot (returns snapshot_id)
  payload: { session_id, reason, sample_policy_id, redaction_level: "hash|partial|none" }

- GET /v1/probe/snapshot/:id (authz guarded)

Probe config (yaml sketch):
probe:
  enabled: true
  mode: sample
  sample_rate: 0.01  # per-route default
  routes:
    "/chat": { sample_rate: 0.02, annotate_only: false }
    "/embed": { sample_rate: 0.001, annotate_only: true }
  retention_seconds: 86400
  redaction: "partial"
  max_snapshot_tokens: 1024
  persist_backend: "ephemeral-store"  # options: ephemeral-store, s3-archival

Privacy and security notes:
- Default to highest redaction when route is classified as "sensitive".
- Provide a pluggable redaction hook: function(context) -> mask spec. Engineers can point to a linear ticket or config id.
- Snapshot IDs rotated daily; access requires role-based access plus request justification header.

Instrumentation and metrics to add:
- probe.added_latency_ms.p50/p90
- probe.snapshots.created_total (by route, by reason)
- probe.sample_rate_applied (effective per-route)
- probe.access_denied_total (audit)

Testing and rollout plan (quick):
1) Unit tests for redaction hooks + property-based fuzzing on mask rules.
2) Local e2e with a small synthetic model (latency guard instrumentation).
3) Canary in dev region: sample_rate = 0.001 for 48h, monitor added_latency & errors.
4) Beta w/ select internal teams (DevX, Solutions) with feedback loop.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to store feature vectors safely if engineers want to attach embeddings? hashed? encrypted at rest?
- Control plane UI: expose a simple per-route toggle or inline policy language?
- SLO for fail-open vs fail-closed — default should be fail-open but some customers may require fail-closed.
- Legal sign-off for snapshot retention > 7d.

Notes to self:
- Keep snapshot payloads under 2KB by default (compress + token-limit).
- Consider a lightweight CLI to fetch snapshot_id and attach to GH/Jira flow.
- Wire up quick play with existing trace-id headers (X-Trace-Id / Redwood-Request-Id).

Example quick debug workflow (for on-call):
1) On alert, enable on-demand capture for route X (control-plane API) or trigger snapshot via header.
2) Snapshot stored ephemeral; on-call fetches snapshot_id and inspects redacted view.
3) If deeper analysis needed, request escalation to persist to long-term store (requires justification).

Approx perf budget: aim for < 4ms p50 added for annotate-only, < 10ms p90 when snapshot triggered (depends on async persist).

If this proves useful, next pass: add a small UI in dev console with quick 'capture' button, snapshot viewer with redaction toggles, and single-click create-Jira (prefill).

-- Diego
